title: fix(superheroes): the worktree guard tells text from a command, and every refusal names its next step
body:
Closes #2064.

Layer 2 of the #2054 stack (part of #2054). It sits on #2065: stack #2078, position 2 of 2, with #2065 at position 1. Both reads below are GitHub's own (`stack_check.py list`). The two layers merge as one stack.

## What's changing, and why

- **The guard stops refusing harmless text, but only in a short list of exact command shapes.** A heredoc whose body merely mentions a git discard is read as text when the whole command is one of these: the heredoc writes a file with `cat >`, `cat >>` or `tee`; it feeds `gh issue|pr … --body-file -` or `git commit -F -`; or it is the whole `git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'` … `)"` or `gh … --body "$(cat <<'EOF'` … `)"` message. The heredoc must have a quoted delimiter, and nothing may come before or after it. Today these refusals stall builds and advisors, including the advisor seat while it was filing #2054.
- **Everything else is checked exactly as it is on main.** That covers anything a shell or interpreter runs, and any shape the guard cannot classify. This is the owner's ruling "106 d": an allowlist, never a parser. It also closes the open Critical from the last review session. That Critical was an escaped quote inside `bash -c` that hid a real discard. The quote-and-escape handling that caused it is gone, and that command is refused again.
- **Every guard refusal now ends with the exact next step.** That means the command or tool to use, and during a merge, the conflict-resolution route from layer 1. The hook's start-up failure text gets the same treatment.

## What we're accepting

- **Text the guard has never looked at is still unchecked, exactly as on main.** A discard written inside a quoted program runs with no guard check. Examples: `bash -c "<discard>"`, `eval "<discard>"`, or a discard inside a double-quoted `$(...)`. This branch does not make that worse, and this PR does not fix it either. It goes to the advisor as FU1.
- **Some harmless text is still refused.** This is the safe direction. Examples are a heredoc followed by `&& git push`, an unquoted delimiter, `gh release`, and a `-m "..."` message holding escaped quotes. In each case the refusal now names the route: write the text with the Write tool and pass the file.
- **The review panel was all one model family** (codex gpt-6.1-sol, per the owner's review-seat pin), so "critical diversity" was relaxed. The panel is still independent of the anthropic-family makers.
- **No reviewer checked this PR body's claims.** The review loop has no phase that runs the grounding seat. The advisor's vet is the check on this body.
- **This leg's work order went out without a fresh brief-check.** The owner's ruling fixed the shape, and the order passed both lint halves.

## How to see it

N/A. This is a **say it** change: a changed refusal rule and refusal texts, stated above. There is nothing to spot-check in an app.

## Advisor vet
<!-- superheroes:advisor-vet -->

**Verdict: READY** · 8f9abae4e2d54ce1f7aa512c6a32c16917a4575a (layer 2; merges whole with #2065)

**What was checked.** Your "106 d" as you ruled it. The guard now lets harmless text through only in a short list of exact shapes: a heredoc written to a file, a `--body-file -` or `commit -F -` heredoc, and the `commit -m` / `--body` message heredoc. Everything else is checked as on main. I fired 14 real commands at the guard in a repo with unsaved work, both on main and on this commit:
- the two heredoc shapes that used to stall builds now pass;
- every real discard is still refused, and the refusal now says what to do instead;
- the serious hole from the last session (a discard hidden inside `bash -c`) is refused.

The review converged in one round, and CI is green.

**What accepting it means.** Builders and advisors stop getting stuck on notes and PR bodies that merely mention a git command. One gap stays exactly as it is on main today: a discard wrapped in `bash -c "…"` or `eval "…"` is not checked. This PR neither causes nor fixes that; item 111 asks whether to file a fix.

**What is yours to decide.** The stack's Merge (#2065 and #2077 merge together, on one sheet). Item 111 is separate.

Receipt: https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/pull/2077#issuecomment-6355853179

**Carried forward 2026-10-23 (merge train):** the head moved from `0fa54f1` to `8f9abae` when the stack was brought current bottom-up with main (c50b6a61, with #2074, #2067, #2084 and #2085); this PR's own changed lines are identical, and CI runs on the new commit before the merge.

<!-- superheroes:build-record -->
<details><summary>Build record</summary>

### Lane, base and head

- **Lane:** full (lane floor: Destroying work, the worktree guard). Presentation: say it.
- **Base:** `fix/2063-refusal-route-merge-guard` at `f631b1bd3` (layer 1, vetted READY).
- **Head:** `0fa54f1fc`, verified on the remote (`git ls-remote`).
- **Stack** (`stack_check.py list`): stack #2078, size 2, base `main`. Position 1 is #2065 at `f631b1bd3`. Position 2 is #2077 at `0fa54f1fc`.
- **Legs:**
  - **Leg 1 (2026-10-22, launch `launch-f8021ac6c188490e`):** WO-C built the first text-versus-command attempt, and a 9-round review-code session ran on it. It ended `capped-with-open-critical` ([record](https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/pull/2077#issuecomment-6348135831), [park](https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/pull/2077#issuecomment-6348289136)).
  - **Leg 2 (this one, launch `launch-42ae0bca68095cd2`):** resumed on the owner's "106 d" ([record](https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/issues/695#issuecomment-6355241482); [resume intake](https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/issues/2054#issuecomment-6355375153)).

### Build brief

The brief is [on #2054](https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/issues/2054) as the "Build brief" comment, and was brief-checked in leg 1. **Change log:**
- 2026-10-22: brief-check folds, then the size split into layers.
- 2026-10-23: owner's "106 d". WO-C's heredoc masking and its escape and substitution handling are replaced by an exact whole-command allowlist (work order D1), and the scanners return to layer 1's text.
  - **Design fork, disclosed:** the `-m "$(cat <<'EOF'` / `--body "$(cat <<'EOF'` message shape is admitted as one exact shape, because that is how the ruling's "`git commit -m` message" and "`gh … --body` argument" entries are written in practice. Plain quoted `-m`/`--body` strings were already treated as text on main and are unchanged.

### Receipts (all re-run by the builder at `0fa54f1fc` unless noted)

- **Bring-current:** layer 1 `f631b1bd3` was merged into layer 2 with a plain `--no-ff` merge (`3a9df7cc1`), with no conflicts. The guard tests on the merge (`pytest plugins/superheroes/lib/tests -k "worktree_guard or command_refusals or refusal" -n auto`) gave **1669 passed**. The stack was already current with main.
- **Calibrated verify:** `validate_python_pin`, `validate_marketplace`, `validate_hosts`, `validate_skills`, `validate_stubs`, all exit 0.
- **Scoped guard suite** (`test_worktree_guard_text.py`, `test_worktree_guard.py`, the EXIT-trap and multiline break-its, `test_worktree_guard_gate_hook.py`, `test_worktree_guard_merge.py`, `test_command_refusals.py`): **430 passed**.
- **Removal census** (`git grep` of the 15 removed names over `plugins/`): no hits. The diff against layer 1 for `worktree_guard.py` touches only the templates, the shared sentences, the new masker and its one call line.
- **CI:** see the handback comment for the run on `0fa54f1fc`. The full local suite was not run; CI is the receipt.

### Review

- **Review session:** one fresh review-code session (`pr 2077`, with the owner's bar in `--focus`). It ran a full `reviewer-deep` panel in round 1: code, security, test and premortem seats, all codex gpt-6.1-sol xhigh. It **converged in round 1**: certification `full-panel-confirmed-degraded` (driver `seat-pin`), independence `independent`.
- **Review record:** https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/pull/2077#issuecomment-6355776618. It reads status `reviewed`, final commit `0fa54f1fc`, 0 left for the owner, 20 findings fixed.

| Finding | Severity | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| test-001: break-it test for a heredoc delimiter that collides with a later discard | Important (proposed test) | The driver ran it at `0fa54f1fc` and it **passed**: the guard refuses the collision. Dropped, nothing to fix. |
| Six leftovers from leg 1: substitution boundaries (two findings), quoted assignments (Critical and Important), the EXIT-trap break-it, and quoted shell programs with escaped quotes | Critical / Important | **Fixed by removal in `0fa54f1fc`.** The builder re-checked each one at the final head with a `classify()` probe (`carried_probe.py`), and the verdicts match the PR base. The EXIT-trap break-it and the `bash -c` escaped-quote test pass. Recorded as `carriedChecks`. |
| The other 14 findings from leg 1 | various | Fixed in leg 1 (see the record). |

### Bite-proof records

The detector is the allowlist masker, `_mask_data_heredoc`. Each guarded condition was disabled by one targeted edit in a detached probe worktree at `0fa54f1fc`. The builder ran the one exact test id red, reverted with the inverse edit, then re-ran green. The implementer's own runs matched.

| Guarded condition | Probe edit | Test | Red | Green |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Quoted delimiter only | `(['"])` → `(['"]?)` in `_HEREDOC_OPERATOR` | `test_near_miss_is_read_as_commands_and_denied[unquoted-delimiter]` | 1 failed | passed |
| Nothing after the terminator | `if False and any(...)` | `[line-after-terminator]` | 1 failed | passed |
| Nothing before the operator line | start `lines` at the first `<<` line | `[line-before-operator-line]` | 1 failed | passed |
| Operator-line character rule | `_CAT_TO_FILE.fullmatch` → `.match` | `[redirected-and-piped-to-sh]` | 1 failed | passed |
| Command-word and shape table | `_words_take_text(...)` → `_words(rest) is not None` | `[bash]` | 1 failed | passed |

All five greens ran in one invocation on the clean file: `5 passed`. Accepted disclosure: the implementer reports that the command-word list cannot be disabled on its own, because the per-shape stdin flag overlaps it. That probe disables the whole `gh`/`git` shape check instead.

### Dispatch provenance

All models below pass the registry gate (`dispatch_guard.py check`).

| Dispatch | Engine / model / effort | Maker family | Result | Refusals |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Order D1, semantic lint (×2) | claude `superheroes:order-linter`, haiku-4.5, medium | — | Pass 1: 2 Important (budget arithmetic; shape M's operator-line rule), both folded. Pass 2: 1 Minor (a locator for `_DENY_INSPECT`), accepted, dispatched without it. | none |
| Order D1, deterministic lint | `order_lint.py check` | — | clean, plus an `order-timeout-missing` warning: the scoped suite runs under 3 minutes and the runner owns the attempt timeout | — |
| D1 implementer (the allowlist, the scanner revert, tests, TRANSITION) | claude, `dispatch-write`, sonnet-5.5, high | anthropic | ok, 1 attempt, 3 of 3 declared items. The issue had already called it a rework of WO-C's surface: the second order on that surface, after the review loop's own fixes. | none |
| Review panel, round 1 (4 seats) | codex, `dispatch-review`, gpt-6.1-sol, xhigh | openai | 3 empty seats with investigated lists, 1 break-it proposal | none |
| Break-it run | review driver, `scripts/pinned-python` | — | passed | — |
| Leg 1 dispatches (WO-A/B/C, brief-check, 9-round review) | see the #2054 brief, the leg-1 record and #2065 | anthropic (implementers, fixer) | — | — |

**Attribution:** leg 1's blocking `bash -c` Critical came from **order quality**. The brief's escape-handling fold (F4) introduced it, not implementer execution.

### Follow-ups for the advisor

Follow-ups: 2 (0 owner-call)
- FU1 [defect] The guard never scans quoted program text. A discard inside `bash -c "…"`, `eval "…"`, or a double-quoted `$(…)` runs unguarded, on main and on this branch alike. It has not been seen in the field. A fix would be a narrow check on shell `-c`/`eval` arguments, its own issue.
- FU2 [craft] Leg 1 dropped two layer-1 test rows: the escaped-quote `--body` row and the opposite-delimiter `$(echo '…')` row. Their behaviour is back, and restoring the rows would pin it again.

### Disclosed degradations

- The panel was single-family, with critical diversity relaxed. Codex-only is the owner's review-seat pin (seat map: `critical-diversity` relaxed).
- The host model was unknown to the session-start hook. The seat map fell back to the anthropic family for the narrative family. The author family comes from the claude implementation engine either way.
- The grounding seat did not run, because no review-loop phase runs it. No reviewer checked this body's claims.
- No new brief-check ran for this leg. The owner's ruling fixed the order's shape. The leg-1 brief was brief-checked, and order D1 passed both lint halves.
